summary: The paper investigates the behavioral impact of transplanting a feed-forward block from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B into Qwen2.5-1.5B on Python repair tasks, tracking the specific repairs gained and lost when the grafted module is ablated. While the study demonstrates commendable methodological transparency by documenting negative results and uncovering a 4-suffix shortcut in the benchmark dataset, the benchmark's vulnerability to suffix shortcuts and single-draw training limit the generalizability of its findings.
strengths: Rigorous inclusion of multiple ablation baselines, including native host, removed feed-forward layer, direct affine replacement, shuffled graft, and general-purpose donor.

Exemplary scientific honesty in reporting null and negative findings, including showing that the general-purpose donor outperformed the coding graft and that the graft's advantage over native host was not statistically significant.
Clear identification and disclosure of a benchmark artifact, specifically noting that a four-entry suffix-only heuristic predicts all 512 evaluation outcomes.
Precise specification of experimental hyperparameters, evaluation seeds, software stack versions (MLX, MLX-LM, NumPy), and hardware environment.
weaknesses: The evaluation benchmark suffers from a critical structural shortcut where four post-gap suffixes determine all outcomes, preventing conclusions about true syntax parsing or nested stack tracking.
The adaptation phase relied on a very small training set of only 16 examples across a single supervised draw, introducing potential training variance.
The primary hypothesis failed pre-registered promotion criteria, showing that grafting domain-specific layers did not meaningfully outperform general-purpose or native adaptations.
suggestions: Redesign the benchmark test suite to decouple post-gap suffixes from correct repair tokens, such as evaluating balanced parentheses and variable scopes across identical suffix triplets.
Run multiple training draws with varying random seeds on the 16 adaptation examples to report variance and confidence intervals over the fitting phase.
Compare the single-block transplant against standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA) on the same host model to establish a competitive baseline.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies layer-stitching concepts to modern decoder-only language models under fill-in-the-middle prompts, specifically auditing token-level repair disappearance under layer ablation.
